items.title: Shared converse: gradient monotonicity implies strong convexity

source.anchor: Lower_Strong_Convex, lines 144–155; ConvexFunction.lean::monotone_gradient_convex' is its upstream convexity dependency
source.attribution: Chenyi Li and Ziyu Wang, Optlib, Apache-2.0. ASTIS mathematical restatement.

items.statement: Let E be a complete real inner-product space, s a convex subset, f:E→ℝ, g:E→E and m∈ℝ. Suppose f has ambient gradient g(z) at every z∈s. If ⟨g(y)−g(x),y−x⟩≥m‖y−x‖² for every x,y∈s, then f is m-strongly convex on s, in the chord sense with quadratic correction m/2.
assumptions: E is a complete real inner-product space, s is a convex subset of E, f:E→ℝ, g:E→E and m∈ℝ.
At every z∈s, g(z) is a genuine ambient gradient: HasGradientAt f (g z) z. This includes boundary points, and implies the continuity needed at segment endpoints.
For every x,y∈s, the gradient difference paired with y−x is at least m‖y−x‖². The modulus may be positive, zero or negative.

formulae.label: Conclusion
formulae.tex: f(ax+by)\le af(x)+bf(y)-\frac m2ab\|x-y\|^2,\quad x,y\in s,\ a,b\ge0,\ a+b=1.

obligations.label: Domain-local gradient inequality implies the strong-convexity chord inequality.

assumption_deltas.source: Complete real inner-product space, convex domain, ambient gradients on the domain; arbitrary real modulus.
assumption_deltas.lean: Identical space/domain/gradient/modulus hypotheses; ordered pairs are written with y−x instead of x−y.
assumption_deltas.reason: Swapping the universally quantified endpoints reconciles the gradient bound without changing the normalization or assumptions.

assumption_deltas.source: Supplied HasGradientAt at every domain point.
assumption_deltas.lean: Continuity on each closed segment and differentiability on its interior are derived from those ambient gradients.
assumption_deltas.reason: No extra regularity hypothesis is added. Measures, representatives, integrability and domination do not apply to this mean-value proof; endpoints are covered by the given gradients.

assumption_deltas.source: Chewi uses Euclidean whole-space C¹ and α≥0 for the corresponding implication.
assumption_deltas.lean: The primary source here is the more general Optlib domain-local supplied-gradient statement with arbitrary m.
assumption_deltas.reason: This comparison explains the intended textbook use, not a source repair or a claim that the integral proof has been reproduced.
